review_notes: I read the whole file and the called lemmas cutoff_radius_factor_thresholds, actual_radiusLevelTime_stopping and phaseAt_regulator_eq_and_le_one. Most statements are tied to the concrete three-stop (Fin 3) structure and ℝ, and I judged that specialisation appropriate. The one weakening I found is in actual_phase_regulator. It is modest: the monotonicity hypothesis horder already encodes the ordering, so the practical gain is small. I did not compile anything. The replacement is just substituting h₂ i for (h₀ i).trans (hu i) in the single call to cutoff_radius_factor_thresholds, and nothing else in that proof uses hu.

findings.excerpt: (h₀ : ∀ i, 0 ≤ u₀ i) (hu : ∀ i, u₀ i ≤ u₂ i)
findings.problem: The hypothesis hu : u₀ i ≤ u₂ i is used in the proof only to derive 0 ≤ u₂ i, via (h₀ i).trans (hu i), which is passed as the h₂ argument of cutoff_radius_factor_thresholds. The statement therefore assumes a stronger ordering condition than it needs. The ordering of the stops is already supplied separately by horder.
findings.proposed_change: Replace `(hu : ∀ i, u₀ i ≤ u₂ i)` by `(h₂ : ∀ i, 0 ≤ u₂ i)`. In the proof, pass `(h₂ i)` instead of `((h₀ i).trans (hu i))` to cutoff_radius_factor_thresholds. Existing callers that have hu can supply `fun i => (h₀ i).trans (hu i)`. The degenerate case u₂ < u₀ with 0 ≤ u₂ is now admitted, and the proof still goes through unchanged.
findings.benefit: The theorem needs only the nonnegativity of the radius levels, so callers do not have to establish or carry an ordering u₀ ≤ u₂ for this result. The hypotheses then match what cutoff_radius_factor_thresholds actually requires.
